summary:
Root owns the delegated facility/operator and first FourD native consumer choices; no further user choice is needed. The explicit route in https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4516#issuecomment-6401617169 selects preparation of a Home-hosted fresh disposable Noble guest for FourD, after the primary runner, bake, registration and first BAR consumer. The FourD target must be on Home. Root also selects a reusable automated Noble desktop route using the existing accessibility owner as script operator and Home as facility executor only when qualified. Ambient Home desktop capabilities do not establish a supported Noble accessibility facility. These are route choices, not a native execution envelope or evidence that the facilities exist.

At the cited c47 source the dedicated runner remains closed to the named private BAR and FourD callers; the shared c068 baseline retains SDK10.0.401/runtime10.0.12. A distinct AT-only workload, caller, provenance, software contract and target label require their actual normal source review and qualification. A public Rendering or Templates caller is not implicitly routed by choosing Home or sharing a guest mechanism. Root remains sole integrator of the shared private qualification receiver, with first BAR adoption ahead of accessibility bootstrap.

The FourD reproducibility repair supplies a separate deterministic side-by-side SDK10.0.400/10.0.401 and runtime10.0.13 profile. Its fixed host digest participates in the exact producer/consumer runtime join; do not weaken that join, substitute an ambient host with a matching version label, modify an old archive or infer native adoption from publication. The selected target still owes actual runtime/path/hash, source-bound consumer artifact and credential/capsule/P2 custody inputs under a separately reviewed finite operation. Producer uploader identity and native consumer actor identity are different facts.

Accessibility still owes the actual assembled Noble desktop, portable game artifact, input method, assistive technology, keymaps, focus behavior, screen-reader/IME journeys and original bounded retirement. Source/DOM/no-install dependency planning cannot supply that acceptance. Where builder and desktop ABI requirements differ, retain source-bound artifact handoff rather than assuming managed-code portability. The reusable Home Arch/glibc2.44 builder remains a preferred separate candidate whose actual tools, native ABI, namespaces, backing and capacity must be proved after the primary runner path. The existing reusable-qualification-facilities record retains that builder contract and budget arithmetic.

Private runtime assets, keys, actor records and raw facility diagnostics remain outside Atlas. This record grants no installation, service change, dispatch, resource reservation, retry or historical release. Refresh actual capability and determining source before selecting a complete operation.
title: Selected Home native routes still require actual facility and source closure
